tytul: Fresh mozzarella stretched in hot water (NMSU recipe)
wstep: This card follows the NMSU Extension “pizza cheese” (mozzarella) recipe: curd made with yogurt as the culture is stretched in hot water at 180 °F (82 °C), brined for 24 hours and kept in the refrigerator for up to a week.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Make this cheese only from pasteurized milk; raw milk must be pasteurized before it is used for cheese.
If you keep the fresh cheese in water, eat it within 2 days.

akapity: The NMSU recipe does not measure pH, so this card gives no pH value.
NMSU uses 1 gallon (3.79 l) of 2% milk, or 2 quarts (1.9 l) of whole milk plus 2 quarts of skim milk.
The culture is 1/4 cup (57 g) of fresh plain yogurt.
The rennet is 1 tablet or 1 teaspoon of liquid rennet, dissolved in 1/2 cup of water.
For the brine, NMSU uses 2 lb (907 g) of salt per gallon (3.78 l) of water.
Heat the milk to 90 °F (32.2 °C), add the yogurt and stir slowly for 15 minutes, keeping that temperature.
Add the dissolved rennet and stir for 3–5 minutes.
Cover and keep at 90 °F (32.2 °C) for about 30 minutes, until the milk has coagulated.
Cut the curd into 1/2-inch (1.27 cm) cubes and leave them for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Raise the temperature slowly to 118 °F (47.7 °C) over 45 minutes and hold it for 15 minutes more.
Let the curd settle, remove the whey and move the mat of curd to a flat pan that you can keep warm.
Do not cut the mat; turn it over every 15 minutes for 2 hours.
Cut the mat into strips 1–2 inches (2.5–5 cm) wide and cover them with hot water at 180 °F (82.2 °C).
With wooden spoons, tumble and stretch the curd under the hot water for about 15 minutes, until it is elastic.
Shape it by hand into a ball or loaf and put it into cold water at 40 °F (4.4 °C) for about 1 hour.
Then put it into saturated brine kept at 40–50 °F (4.4–10 °C), in a heavy plastic, glass or pottery container.
Cover any exposed parts of the cheese with salt or brine and leave it in the brine for 24 hours.
Take it out, let it dry for several hours, wrap it in plastic wrap or a sealable bag and refrigerate it.
Brined and wrapped, the cheese keeps in the refrigerator for up to a week.
Cheese kept in water must be eaten within 2 days.
Pregnant women should avoid cheeses made from unpasteurized milk.
